question: Why OpenHOI3 pulled Germany's 14th and 26th Corps towards 1485 at 08:00 on 17 July 1941.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::OrganiseCommands
addresses.comment:
**Slot 85: the agent's daily reorganisation of the land order of battle under its unit**, run by CAIUnit::Tick at hour `(country id + 3) % 24`. 0x4C20C0 to the bare `ret` at 0x4C276E; answers whether it posted anything. Nothing unless the agent has a unit (+0x64) and an area (GetArea, a CTheatre).

1. Where the owner's AI runs units (`CEU3AI +0x2C`) or the unit's plan allows headquarters reorganisation (`CUnit +0x205`, CUnitPlan +0x9 `allow_hq_reorg`): CAIUnit_CreateHigherCommands (0x4C2CD0) - the new corps, armies and army groups.
2. Over the land units of the subtree (`+0x11C`, slot 78's list, CArmy*): each has `CUnit +0x2C4` (pending subordinates) zeroed; the agent's own unit, a unit carried by a fleet (`CArmy +0x300`) and one slot 86 answers true for are skipped; the rest are sorted by oob_level into army groups (1), armies (2), corps (3), and the rest - a level 0 or 4 unit whose first brigade (0x1BD220) is the `garrison_brigade` type into a garrison list, any other into a list of divisions.
3. Under the same gate as 1: every garrison division whose parent is not the agent's unit is attached straight under it (CAttachUnitCommand(division, unit); the old parent's +0x2C4 down one, the unit's up one), and so is every fleet of the subtree (slot 78's `+0xDC`) whose parent is not the agent's unit.
4. CAIUnit::AssignToNearestCommand (0x4C2770) three times: divisions to corps, corps to armies, armies to army groups.

The four RADIO_*_LEADER_DISTANCE reads the record placed here are in 0x4C2770, not in this body. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agents.md, section B. **Seen in play 2026-11-15** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 98): Germany's 1. Fallschirmjäger Division, aboard the 14th Air wing with staging_province 5138 in the July 1941 save, is skipped by step 2's slot-86 test and stays under the 26th Corps through the run.
addresses.evidence: The division's parent read from every save of a run; the 14th Corps' children as the pull-in's reach test met them on the running game.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_PullHeadquartersIn
addresses.comment: **Moves the agent's headquarters to stand among their subordinates.** 0x4CC320 to `ret 4`, called by CAIUnit::Tick at hour `(id + 6) % 24` or while `+0x84` is set. Over the agent's non-division units (`+0x14C`), skipping its own unit, one retreating (+0x158), and one in a battle (+0x11C) it may not leave (CUnit::MayLeaveCombats, 0x1C0000): **a unit on the move is always looked at**; one standing still only where some child is reached by less than its full command (CUnit::CommandReachFrom under 1000), or it is trespassing (+0x1A8), or it stands on a front province (IsFrontProvince(false)) while the agent's `+0x364` is set. target = CAIUnit_PickProvinceAmongSubordinates(agent, unit) (0x4DA660); where it is not null, not where the unit is going (or standing), and CMapProvince::CanUnitReach(target, unit, 1, 1): CEU3AI::MoveUnit(owner, unit, target, 0, 1, 1, null). Answers whether it moved one. On the listing (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 47): 'where the unit is going (or standing)' is EBX - 0x7AAF00's destination for a moving unit (0x4CC38E), else +0x130 after the standing tests (0x4CC3E9) - compared at 0x4CC3FF. **Live 2026-11-11** (section 48): a land unit slot 78 let slot 86 claim is not on +0x14C at all, so is never looked at - Italy's III Corpo d'Armata dell'A.O.I. entering April 1936, Britain's 7th Army entering July 1941. **Its agent is the stack argument** ([ebp+8], 0x4CC326), not ECX. **Logged 2026-11-15** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 98) at the take (0x4CC35E, unit in ESI) and the reach test (call 0x4CC3B2 with the child at [ESP] and the headquarters at [ESP+8], figure at [EAX] after 0x4CC3B7): at 08:00 on 17 July 1941 Germany's 14th Corps has every child at 1000 and is not pulled in; the 26th Corps' 208. Infanterie-Division is at 0, its pick 2041.
addresses.evidence: Breakpoints at 0x4CC35E, 0x4CC3B2 and 0x4CC3B7 over the hour, every German headquarters logged.
